channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Syrian FM: Israel struck airbase despite assurances no Turkish base was planned
item.description: Syrian FM Asaad Al-Shaibani tells Axios that Israel struck Abu al-Duhur airbase despite assurances Syria had no plans for a permanent Turkish military presence.

item.title: Report: US opens secret Hormuz oil corridor
item.description: US forces have established a secret Hormuz shipping corridor moving millions of oil barrels daily, according to an Axios report.

item.title: Australia 'outraged' as Israel rules out criminal probe into WCK strike
item.description: Australia 'outraged' as Israel rules out criminal probe into WCK strike

item.title: Tel Aviv shopping center distances itself from 'Palestinian state' sign
item.description: Left-wing activists hang a sign calling for the establishment of a Palestinian state without authorization. Dizengoff Center removes it and calls police.

item.title: 60-year-old critically injured after falling from balcony in Jerusalem
item.description:
A man in his 60s was critically injured and in unstable condition after falling from a balcony approximately four meters above the ground in Jerusalem.
United Hatzalah teams provided him with initial medical treatment before he was evacuated to the hospital.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan set to move back to UK with their children
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan are preparing to move back to the UK later this month, according to British media, with their children set to attend a British school in September.

item.title: Man in his 50s missing for hours found dead on Ashkelon beach
item.description:
Magen David Adom (MDA) confirmed that a man in his 50s who had been missing for several hours was found dead at the National Park Beach in Ashkelon.
MDA medical teams pronounced him dead at the scene.

item.title: Trump declares 'economic D-Day' against Iran
item.description: President Trump announces an unprecedented economic campaign against Iran, threatening severe consequences for countries and businesses that aid Tehran.

item.title: Death toll from Colombia earthquake rises to 314
item.description:
The death toll from the earthquake that struck Colombia last week has risen to 314, President Abelardo de la Espriella announced.
According to the president, 262 people are still reported missing.

item.title: Trump: Hormuz blockade is '100% successful'
item.description: President Trump says the Hormuz blockade is "100% successful" as negotiations with Iran remain stalled and warns Tehran could face severe sanctions.

item.title: On the verge of history: Hapoel Be’er Sheva wins 2-1
item.description:
Hapoel Be’er Sheva defeated Azerbaijan’s Sabah 2-1 and is now just 90 minutes away from reaching the Champions League for the first time in the club’s history.
Javon East and Igor Zlatanović scored to complete the comeback against the Azerbaijani champions.

item.title: Chief Rabbi to Eisenkot: A source of inspiration
item.description: At an event marking the dedication of a memorial and study room for Israel’s fallen soldiers, the Chief Rabbi shakes Gadi Eisenkot’s hand and tells him, “You are a source of inspiration."

item.title: The Joint List returns, without Ra’am
item.description: Representatives of Hadash, Ta’al and Balad agree to run together in the upcoming elections. Ra’am will not be part of the alliance.

item.title: Bereaved families against Trump admin. meetings with Hamas: 'Fight terrorism, don’t talk to it'
item.description:
Bereaved families from the Gevurah Forum have launched a campaign against negotiations with senior Hamas officials, amid Jared Kushner’s visit to Israel and contacts being held by representatives of the Trump administration.
The bereaved families distributed advertisements under the headline, “You fight terrorism, you don’t talk to it," sharply criticizing Kushner for engaging in talks with the organization’s leadership.
The campaign prominently features Khalil al-Hayya, a senior Hamas official and one of the key figures in the organization’s leadership involved in the negotiations currently underway.

item.title: After 44 years: Yehuda Katz to be laid to rest on Friday
item.description:
The funeral of Staff Sgt. Yehuda Yekutiel Katz, who fell in the Battle of Sultan Yacoub and whose remains were returned to Israel this week, will be held on Friday.
The funeral procession will depart from Kerem B’Yavneh Yeshiva and proceed to the military section of the cemetery on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem.

item.title: Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu warns: “A full dictatorship"
item.description: Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu was asked by his son, Minister Amichai Eliyahu, whether the judicial reform should be abandoned in favor of a unity government.

item.title: 125 mph in the dark: Police chase ends at spike strip
item.description: A 19-year-old new driver was arrested after allegedly reaching 201 km/h on Route 60, shutting off his lights and trying to flee police.

item.title: Why are they hosting a pundit who accused Jews of buying Congress?
item.description: If a white supremacist accused Jews of bribing members of Congress, no synagogue would invite him as a speaker. New York's oldest Reform Jewish congregation is hosting a newspaper columnist who has made that exact same accusation. Opinion.

item.title: After captivity and the fight to bring him home: Eliya Cohen and Ziv Abud marry tonight
item.description: After ten years together, 505 days during which Eliya Cohen was held hostage, and a prolonged struggle to bring him home, he and Ziv Abud are getting married tonight.

item.title: Report: Mossad Chief spoke with Syrian FM days before Israeli airstrikes
item.description: Mossad chief Roman Gofman reportedly spoke with Syria’s foreign minister days before Israel struck an airbase, warning against Turkey’s military presence.

item.title: Israel's first Bedouin judge under threat
item.description: Judge Nasser Abu Taha, who became Israel’s first Bedouin judge, has requested to relocate from his home in southern Israel to the north and serve there following threats.

item.title: Lebanon Talks: Israel demands return of fallen prisoners’ remains
item.description: Israel reportedly demands the return of Israeli prisoners’ remains as talks with Lebanon continue, with Hezbollah refusing to leave a key southern Lebanon position.

item.title: IDF strikes terrorists meeting in Gaza police station
item.description:
Following the strikes earlier today (Wednesday), the IDF and ISA struck a gathering of terrorists in a police station in the Tuffah area of the northern Gaza Strip. During the strike, at least four terrorists from Hamas' military wing were present, alongside another terrorist from the military wing of the Popular Resistance Committees terrorist organization. The IDF will provide further updates on the result of the strike when possible.
The IDF emphasized that the terrorists who were struck operated from a civilian police station to advance terror attacks against IDF troops in the Gaza Strip, while using it for military purposes and against international law.
Prior to the strike, steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians.
Half an hour before then, a platoon commander from the Hamas terrorist organization, who infiltrated Israeli territory during the October 7th Massacre, was eliminated. The IDF will provide further updates on his terror activity when possible.

item.title: IDF eliminates Hamas commanders involved in October 7 and Gaza attacks
item.description: IDF identifies four Nukhba commanders eliminated in a northern Gaza strike, including an October 7 infiltrator and three involved in attacks on troops.

item.title: Shalom Leon, father of Jerusalem Mayor, dies at 92
item.description: Shalom Leon, who immigrated to Israel before the Holocaust, passed away at Ichilov Hospital. His funeral will take place Thursday in Givatayim.

item.title: West Nile Virus carrying mosquitoes detected in several areas
item.description:
The Health and Environmental Protection Ministries announced that mosquitoes carrying the West Nile virus were detected in the areas of Petah Tikva, Kafr Qasim, Kafr Bara, Ben Gurion Airport, and the Brenner and Central Arava regional councils.
Since the beginning of the season, 17 people have been diagnosed with the virus. One person has died, while another remains hospitalized.

item.title: Southern Hebron Hills fire: Four firefighting planes working to contain the blaze, Route 60 closed
item.description:
The wildfire near the community of Afeka in the Southern Hebron Hills continues to spread rapidly through woodland and open areas.
Four firefighting aircraft are operating to contain the blaze before it reaches residential homes, while additional support teams are on their way to the scene. Highway 60 in the area of the fire has been closed to traffic in both directions.

item.title: Chief of Staff in Syria: 'We won't allow enemeies to establish themselves on our borders'
item.description: LTG Eyal Zamir tours security zone in southern Syria, warns escalation could develop on any front and praises reservists who have served hundreds of days since the war began.
